title: Manage and secure Power BI: workspaces, sharing, refresh and governance

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and items
questions.stem: Select the least-privileged workspace role for each person.

parts.label: Can delete the workspace and add other Admins
Publishes and edits reports but doesn't share or manage the app
Publishes and updates the workspace app and adds Contributors
Only reads and interacts with reports

questions.explanation: Viewer can only view and interact. Contributor can create, edit and delete content. Member can also share, publish or update the app, and add Members, Contributors and Viewers. Only Admin can delete the workspace, change its settings or add Admins.
questions.takeaway: View → Viewer. Edit → Contributor. Share/app/add people → Member. Settings/delete/Admins → Admin.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and items
questions.stem:
The exhibit shows a workspace's Manage access panel. Priya must be able to add other people to the workspace, using the least privilege.

Which role should Priya have?

image.alt: Manage access for the Sales Analytics workspace: Finance Admins group as Admin, Priya Nair as Contributor (selected), Sales Team group as Viewer.

questions.explanation: Contributors can't add people. Members can add Members, Contributors and Viewers, which meets the requirement without the extra rights of Admin.
questions.takeaway: Add people (not Admins) → Member.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and items
questions.stem:
Several people need the same workspace role, and staff join and leave often.

What is the best way to grant access?

options.text: Share the workspace link by email
Add a security group to the role

questions.explanation: Assign the role to a Microsoft Entra security group (or Microsoft 365 group). Membership changes are then handled by the group, not by editing workspace access.
questions.takeaway: Grant access to groups, not individuals.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and items
questions.stem:
A workspace is on shared capacity (Pro). Free-licensed users report that they can't open its reports.

What would let free users view the content without buying each of them a Pro licence?

options.text: Move the workspace to Premium per user
Share the reports with Publish to web
Give the users the Viewer role
Move the workspace to Premium capacity or Fabric F64 or larger

questions.explanation: On shared capacity, both creators and viewers need Pro (or PPU) licences. Content in a workspace on Premium capacity (P SKU) or Fabric capacity F64 or larger can be viewed by free users. Premium per user doesn't help, since every viewer would need PPU.
questions.takeaway: Free viewers → content on P SKU or F64+ capacity.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and items
questions.stem:
An analyst publishes reports to My workspace and wants colleagues to collaborate on them.

What should the analyst do?

options.text: Create a shared workspace and publish there
Give colleagues the Viewer role in My workspace

questions.explanation: My workspace is for personal content; you can't add collaborators to it. Create a shared workspace, assign roles, and publish there.
questions.takeaway: Collaboration → a shared workspace, not My workspace.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and items
questions.stem:
You want report and semantic model definitions in a workspace to be version-controlled, with changes committed to a repository.

What should you configure?
questions.explanation: Git integration connects a workspace to an Azure DevOps or GitHub repository, so items can be committed, compared and restored. Saving copies of .pbix files by hand doesn't give real version history.
questions.takeaway: Version control for workspace items → Git integration.

questions.stem:
You publish a workspace app. Later you update a report in the workspace, but app users still see the old version.

What should you do?

options.text: Reinstall the app for each user

questions.explanation: An app is a published snapshot. Changes in the workspace reach app users only when someone with the right role selects Update app.
questions.takeaway: Workspace changes reach app users only after Update app.

questions.stem:
The exhibit shows an app's audience setup. The Finance audience must not see the Pipeline report.

What should you do?

image.alt: App audience settings with Sales and Finance audiences. Finance is selected and currently sees Revenue Overview, Pipeline and Budget vs Actual.

options.text: Hide the Pipeline report in the Finance audience

questions.explanation: In the Finance audience, hide the Pipeline report (each audience controls which content its members see). Content hidden from an audience is still available to other audiences.
questions.takeaway: Different content per group in one app → audiences.

questions.stem:
App users want to build their own reports in Excel and Power BI Desktop using the app's semantic model.

What should you set when publishing the app?

options.text: Allow users to build content with the semantic models in the app permissions

questions.explanation: In the app's permissions, allow audience members to build content with the underlying semantic models. That grants Build permission without giving them a workspace role.
questions.takeaway: App users building their own content → allow Build in app permissions.

questions.stem: Why distribute content to a large audience through an app rather than giving everyone a workspace role?

options.text: Apps separate a curated view for readers from the working workspace

questions.explanation: Apps give readers a curated, navigable package, separate what they see from work in progress in the workspace, and support audiences. Workspace roles are for people who work on the content.
questions.takeaway: Consumers → app. Creators → workspace roles.

questions.stem:
You share a report with a colleague and want them to view it but not share it with anyone else.

What should you do in the share dialog?

options.text: Clear Allow recipients to share this report

questions.explanation: Clear Allow recipients to share this report. They can view and interact but can't reshare. Build permission is a separate check box.
questions.takeaway: Stop resharing → clear the reshare option when sharing.

questions.stem: Select the sharing approach for each requirement.

parts.label: Show a report inside an internal SharePoint Online page, respecting each viewer's access
Publish public census statistics on the company's public website
Let a partner company's staff view a report securely with their own work accounts

questions.explanation: Publish to web makes a report public to anyone with the link, with no sign-in or security, so it's only for public data. Embedding in SharePoint Online keeps Power BI sign-in and permissions. Microsoft Entra B2B guest access lets external partners sign in with their own accounts.
questions.takeaway: Public data → Publish to web. Intranet → SharePoint embed. External partners → B2B guests.

questions.stem:
A colleague asks for a Publish to web link for a report that contains customer revenue.

What should you advise?

options.text: Don't use it: anyone with the link could see the data, with no sign-in
It's fine, because Publish to web respects RLS
It's fine if the link is sent only by email
Use it, but set a sensitivity label

questions.explanation: Publish to web creates a public link that anyone on the internet can open without signing in, and it can't apply RLS. It's only for data meant to be public. Use sharing, an app or a secure embed instead.
questions.takeaway: Publish to web = public internet. Never for confidential data.

questions.stem:
A user wants to analyse a published semantic model in an Excel PivotTable connected live to it.

What do they need?

options.text: Build permission on the semantic model

questions.explanation: Analyze in Excel connects Excel to the semantic model and requires Build permission (or a workspace role that includes it). The PivotTable then uses the model's measures, and RLS applies.
questions.takeaway: Analyze in Excel → Build permission on the semantic model.

questions.stem:
You need to see everyone who has access to a semantic model, including access through apps and direct sharing, and remove one person's Build permission.

Where should you go?

options.text: The semantic model's Manage permissions page

questions.explanation: The semantic model's Manage permissions page lists direct access, access through apps and links, with each person's permissions (Read, Build, Reshare), and lets you remove them.
questions.takeaway: Review and change item-level access → Manage permissions.

questions.stem:
Managers want a report page emailed to them every Monday at 8 AM, with the page attached as a PDF.

What should you create?

options.text: A Power Automate flow with no trigger

questions.explanation: A report subscription emails a snapshot of selected pages on a schedule and can attach the report as PDF or PowerPoint. Alerts are triggered by thresholds, not schedules.
questions.takeaway: Scheduled emails of report pages → subscription.

questions.stem:
Each regional manager should receive the same subscription email, but filtered to their own region, without you creating one subscription per manager.

What should you use?
questions.explanation: A dynamic per-recipient subscription reads recipients and their filter values (such as Region) from a semantic model table, so each person gets their own filtered version from a single subscription.
questions.takeaway: One subscription, personalised per person → dynamic per-recipient subscription.

questions.stem:
A data alert on a dashboard card fires when sales drop below 1 million. The operations team also wants a Teams message posted automatically each time.

What should you do?

options.text: Trigger a Power Automate flow from the alert
Subscribe the Teams channel to the report

questions.explanation: Data alerts can trigger a Power Automate flow (using the Power BI alert trigger), which can post to Teams, send emails or start other processes.
questions.takeaway: Act automatically on an alert → Power Automate.

questions.stem:
You want a dashboard tile that shows an entire report page, including its slicers, and stays interactive.

What should you pin?
questions.explanation: Pin a live page: the whole page becomes one tile that updates and keeps the page's slicers and interactions within the tile. Pinning individual visuals creates separate static tiles, and slicers can't be pinned alone.
questions.takeaway: Whole interactive page on a dashboard → pin a live page.

questions.stem:
A dashboard tile's title must change, and clicking the tile should open a different report page than the one it was pinned from.

Where do you change these?

options.text: Edit the original visual and re-pin

questions.explanation: Tile details (from the tile's More options) let you change the title and subtitle and set a custom link, such as another report page or a web address.
questions.takeaway: Change a tile's title or click target → Edit details on the tile.

questions.stem:
Finance needs an invoice-style report that prints cleanly across many pages, with headers repeated on every page.

Which tool do you use to create it?
questions.explanation: Paginated reports are built in Power BI Report Builder. They're designed for pixel-perfect, page-by-page layouts that print and export reliably, with repeating headers and footers.
questions.takeaway: Printable, multi-page layouts → paginated report in Power BI Report Builder.

questions.stem: Which requirement is the clearest sign you need a paginated report rather than a Power BI report?

options.text: Users drill down and cross-filter visuals
A 300-page customer statement, exported to Word and Excel with exact layout

questions.explanation: Paginated reports suit operational outputs that run to many pages, such as statements or invoices, and need exports to Word, Excel, CSV or XML with exact layout. Interactive exploration is what Power BI reports do best.
questions.takeaway: Many printable pages and exact exports → paginated.

questions.stem:
A paginated report must let users choose a customer before it runs, then show only that customer's statement.

What should you add?
questions.explanation: Report parameters prompt users for values (here a customer) and filter the dataset query. They're the main way to make paginated reports interactive.
questions.takeaway: Paginated report filtering by user choice → report parameter.

questions.stem:
The exhibit shows a semantic model's refresh history.

What has Power BI done after the latest failure, and why?

image.alt: Refresh history with four scheduled refreshes from 6 to 9 October that each failed with invalid credentials, followed by a row saying the schedule was disabled after too many consecutive failures.

options.text: Retried every hour until it succeeded
Turned off scheduled refresh because it failed four times in a row

questions.explanation: After four consecutive scheduled refresh failures, Power BI disables the refresh schedule and notifies the owner. Fix the cause (here, credentials), then turn the schedule back on.
questions.takeaway: Four consecutive failures → schedule disabled.

questions.stem:
A semantic model uses an on-premises SQL Server through a gateway. Refresh fails with 'The data source is missing a gateway connection'.

What should you do?

options.text: Map the data source to a gateway connection in the semantic model's settings

questions.explanation: In the semantic model's settings, under Gateway and cloud connections, map the data source to a gateway connection (creating the connection on the gateway first if needed). Republishing doesn't create the mapping.
questions.takeaway: Missing gateway connection → map the source to a connection in the model's settings.

questions.stem:
Several critical semantic models depend on one on-premises gateway server. If it goes down, all refreshes fail.

What should you set up?

options.text: A personal-mode gateway for each analyst
Additional gateway members in a cluster

questions.explanation: A gateway cluster: install additional gateway members in the same cluster on other servers, so refreshes continue if one member is unavailable.
questions.takeaway: Gateway high availability → a gateway cluster.

questions.stem:
A semantic model must refresh as soon as the nightly ETL (extract, transform, load) job finishes, which varies between 2 AM and 5 AM.

What should you use?

options.text: Trigger the refresh when the ETL job completes

questions.explanation: Trigger the refresh when the job finishes, for example from the ETL pipeline or a Power Automate flow calling the refresh action or API. A fixed schedule would either run too early or wait unnecessarily.
questions.takeaway: Refresh after an upstream job → trigger it (pipeline, Power Automate or API).

questions.stem:
The exhibit shows lineage view. You plan to remove a column from the Sales semantic model.

What should you check first?

image.alt: Lineage view: SQL Server feeds the Sales semantic model, which feeds the Sales Overview and Regional Detail reports; Sales Overview feeds the Exec Dashboard.

options.text: Impact analysis for the semantic model

questions.explanation: Impact analysis on the semantic model shows downstream reports, dashboards and workspaces that depend on it (and lets you notify their contacts), so you can see what the change might break. Lineage view already shows two reports and a dashboard downstream.
questions.takeaway: Before changing a shared model → impact analysis.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem: Select the endorsement that fits each situation.

parts.label: The model's owner thinks it's ready for others to reuse
A governance team has reviewed the model against company standards
The single authoritative source of customer reference data

questions.explanation: Promoted means the owner thinks the item is ready to share. Certified means an authorised reviewer has checked it against organisational standards. Master data marks the authoritative source for core reference data, such as the customer master list.
questions.takeaway: Promoted = owner's endorsement. Certified = official review. Master data = core reference data.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem: Who can certify a semantic model?

options.text: People authorised by the admin in the tenant's certification setting

questions.explanation: Only users or groups the Power BI (Fabric) admin has authorised in the tenant's certification setting can certify content. Workspace roles alone aren't enough.
questions.takeaway: Certify → people authorised in tenant settings.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and items
questions.stem:
The exhibit shows a deployment pipeline. You changed one report in Development.

What happens when you deploy from Development to Test?

image.alt: Deployment pipeline: Development (1 item changed), Test and Production, each with a Sales model and two reports. Development and Test are marked Different; Test and Production are marked Same.

options.text: The change goes straight to Production
The changed content is copied to the Test workspace
Only the data is copied, not the report

questions.explanation: Deploying copies the selected (or changed) content from the source stage to the target stage's workspace. The comparison indicator shows the stages differ. Production is untouched until you deploy from Test.
questions.takeaway: Deploy = copy content to the next stage's workspace; later stages are unaffected.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and items
questions.stem:
In a deployment pipeline, the Production stage must automatically use the production database and a parameter value of Prod.

What should you configure?

options.text: Deployment rules for the Production stage

questions.explanation: Deployment rules on the Production stage (data source rules and parameter rules) change the connection and parameter values whenever content is deployed into that stage.
questions.takeaway: Per-stage connections or parameters → deployment rules.

questions.topic: Create and manage workspaces and items
questions.stem: Which workspaces can be assigned to deployment pipeline stages?

options.text: Workspaces on Premium per user, Premium or Fabric capacity

questions.explanation: Deployment pipelines need workspaces on Premium per user, Premium capacity or Fabric capacity. Shared-capacity (Pro) workspaces can't be assigned to stages.
questions.takeaway: Deployment pipelines → Premium, PPU or Fabric workspaces.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
Your organisation requires every report and semantic model to have a sensitivity label before it's saved or published.

What should the admin configure?
questions.explanation: A mandatory labeling policy (set up in Microsoft Purview and enabled for Power BI) forces users to apply a label. A default label can also be applied automatically, but mandatory labeling is what enforces the requirement.
questions.takeaway: Labels required → mandatory labeling policy.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem: A report has the Highly Confidential label, which includes encryption. For each statement, select Yes if it is true.
statements: An exported Excel file keeps the label's protection.
Labels can be applied in Power BI Desktop as well as in the service.
The label restricts which rows each user sees in the report.
questions.explanation: Supported exports, such as Excel, PowerPoint and PDF, carry the label and its protection, so only authorised people can open them. Labels are defined in Microsoft Purview and applied in Power BI Desktop or the service. A label doesn't filter rows; that's RLS.
questions.takeaway: Labels classify and protect exported files; they don't filter data.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
A semantic model has the Confidential label. You create a new report on it in the service.

What happens to the report's label?

options.text: The report has no label until someone adds one
The report inherits the Confidential label

questions.explanation: With downstream inheritance enabled, new content created from a labelled semantic model inherits its label (unless a label was set manually). This keeps classification consistent.
questions.takeaway: Downstream inheritance → new content inherits the model's label.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
An admin wants to stop users from exporting underlying data from reports across the organisation.

Where is this controlled?

options.text: Tenant settings in the admin portal

questions.explanation: Export settings are tenant settings in the admin portal (with options such as allowing only summarized data). Report authors can also restrict export per report, but organisation-wide control is in tenant settings.
questions.takeaway: Organisation-wide export rules → admin portal tenant settings.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
You need to know how often a report was viewed in the last 30 days and by how many users.

What should you open?
questions.explanation: The report's usage metrics report shows views, unique viewers and page usage over recent days. Lineage view and refresh history don't track viewing.
questions.takeaway: Who's viewing → usage metrics.

questions.topic: Secure and govern Power BI items
questions.stem:
A semantic model in another workspace must be used by your report, but you don't have a role in that workspace.

Which permission lets you connect to it from Power BI Desktop?

options.text: The Viewer role in your own workspace
Build permission on the semantic model

questions.explanation: Build permission on the semantic model lets you discover it, connect from Desktop (as a live connection or composite model) and build reports, without any role in its workspace.
questions.takeaway: Use someone else's model → Build permission.
